contexts.text: As the must is found in the cluster... (); the cluster = charity; the must = the goods and derivative truths of charity.
Scortation, and wine, and must hath possessed the heart ()... Wine = falsity; must = the derivative evil.

Multitude of corn and must () = the derivative natural good, and the derivative natural truth... Must = truth; which, when predicated of the Natural, = natural truth; and then... wine is predicated of the Rational.
That corn and must = these things. Illustrated.
A drought upon the must () = a defect of truth.
A land of corn and of must () = the good and truth of the Church.
The must shall mourn () = that truth will cease.
Corn and must () = good and the derivative truth.
With corn and must have I sustained him () = the good and truth thereof.
The must () = the truth of the Church.
The must in the cluster () = truth from good in the Natural.
The derivative goods of love and of charity are signified by that the mountains shall drop must, and the hills shall flow away ().
The good of faith is the winepress, the must, and the libation of wine ().
They shall be inebriated with their blood as with must ().
The first-fruits of the vintage were those of wine, must, and oil. AC 9223:end, Explained.
To tread the must, but not to drink the wine () = to be instructed concerning the truths which are from good, but still not to appropriate them to one's self. AC 9277:2.
The vine said unto them. Shall I make to cease my must, gladdening God and men ().
Howl, all ye drinkers of wine, on account of the must which is cut off from your mouth (). AR 316:2.

It is said that He would take his corn, his must, his wool, and his flax, with which he had covered his nakedness (), because by corn is signified the interior good of the Spiritual Church; by the must, its interior truth; by the wool, its exterior good; and by the flax, its exterior truth.
By must is signified all the truth of the Church. Reference.
That must = the derivative truth. Reference.
Like ferments put into meals and musts, by means of which the heterogeneous things are separated, and the homogeneous ones are conjoined...
Holy truth is signified by must, and wine, in other places also in the Word. Illustrated.
Scortation = the falsification of truth; in like manner, here () wine, and must.

A winepress = exploration, because in winepresses the must is expressed from the clusters, and the oil from the olives; and from the expressed must and oil is perceived of what quality the clusters and olives had been.
For by the blood out of the winepress is meant the must and wine from the trodden clusters; and by the must and wine like things are signified.
Being gladdened with the most delicate musts of grapes.
Others were expressing the must from grapes, cherries, and berries into cups, and drinking jovially.
Musta vinorum concreta.
As the dregs precipitate themselves to the bottom when the must of wine is clarified.
The unition of spiritual things with natural ones, and the derivative appearance of life in material ones, may be compared to noble wine in a clean sponge, and to the saccharine must in the grape...
After he has poured libations of must to demons.
Like those who mix poison with musts...
(The love of the world) is like the must of unfermented wine, which tastes sweet, but infests the belly.
Where all the hills would flow with generous musts.
(Butterflies) eat the must of flowers.
Wine = interior falsity; must () = exterior falsity.
Occurs. AE 340:14. AE 638:20.
That spiritual good would cease, is signified by that the must shall mourn... For by must is signified spiritual good.
The multiplication of good and truth is meant by, Their corn and must are multiplied (). Corn = good; and must, truth.
Wheat = the good of the natural man; must (), its truth.
By corn is meant the good of every kind in the external man; by must (), the truth also there.
By must and oil () are signified truth and good.
By must and oil () are signified the truth and good of the Church. AE 543:9.
Must () = truth; and oil, good.
Must () = truth; and oil, good.
By the mountains shall drop must, or wine () is meant that from the good of love to the Lord is all genuine truth. AE 405:7. AE 405:19. AE 433:13. AE 483:5.
Corn and must () = all the good and truth of the Church.
By the corn, must, and oil which they should gather () are signified all the good and truth of the external and internal man.
By to live in a land of corn and must () is signified [to live] in all the good and truth of the Church.
By wheat, must, and oil () are signified goods and truths of every kind.
By the must which the sons of the stranger shall not drink () is signified in general the truth of the Church, which shall no longer be consumed by... falsities.
That they will not profit by the hearing of these things, is signified by... the must shall lie to them ().
By wine, and must () is meant the truth of the Church. AE 543:9.
By the must which shall mourn and by the vine which shall languish () is signified all the truth of the Church, (and) its deprivation. AE 618:4.
The derivative falsity is signified by must ().
Must () = the truth of the Word; and the vine, the truth of doctrine of the Church.
By they shall gather corn and must () is signified instruction in the goods and truths of doctrine and of the Church.
The spiritual and celestial good and truth which the man of the Church has thence, are meant by the corn, must, and oil which they will gather ().

That thence they have the truth and good of love to the Lord, is signified by that the winepresses shall overflow with must and oil (). ( = that from the good of charity they have truth and its delight. AE 922:6.)
The must shall lie to her = that neither shall there be any truth of good; for must, like wine = truth from the good of charity and of love.
By corn and must () are signified all the good and truth in the natural man.
Corn makes the youths grow up, and must the virgins () = that the understanding of truth, and the affection of truth, are formed through good and through truth from the Lord.
